data.name: Khak
data.gender_notes: Khak is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Khak’ meaning soil or earth. In Islamic tradition, the soil is a symbol of the connection between the human being and the earth, reminding us of our humble origins and the importance of living in harmony with nature. The name Khak carries the meaning “Soil, Earth” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Khak usually hope their child will grow to embody soil, earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the connection between the human being and the earth, emphasizing humility, respect for nature, and the importance of living in harmony with the natural world.
data.etymology: Khak belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soil, Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khak total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.
